title: Keeping our Workers and Workplaces Safe
what_it_is: Keeping our Workers and Workplaces Safe

sections.label: Workplace fatality rate trends
sections.summary: The workplace fatality rate fell from 1.9 per 100,000 workers in 2016 to 1.1 in 2019, then spiked in 2021 as companies cleared pandemic backlogs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Pre-COVID-19, we were witnessing a downward trend for workplace fatalities, where the workplace fatality rate had dropped from 1.9 per 100,000 workers in 2016, to 1.1 per 100,000 workers in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2021, we saw a spike in workplace accidents, injuries and fatalities, as companies rushed to clear the backlog of work caused by the pandemic.

sections.label: MOM actions and Labour Movement proposals
sections.summary: MOM increased inspections, doubled maximum composition fines, required external auditors and is developing an Approved Code of Practice, while the Labour Movement proposes five action areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Before I suggest how we can do better, let me first acknowledge what MOM has done in recent months to address the rise in workplace fatalities and injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: It is important to acknowledge that MOM has: one, increased the number of safety inspections; two, doubled the maximum composition fine for offences observed during inspections; three, required companies that have been issued stop-work orders or have had workers sustained major injuries to engage external auditors to review their WSH practices; and four, is developing an Approved Code of Practice for Company Directors' WSH Duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement, therefore, proposes five action areas to further improve WSH practices: one, establish safe and easy-to-use Reporting channels; two, partner the unions to enhance safety Inspections; three, step up safety Gearing of our workers; four, mandate Higher management's commitment to safety; and five, leverage Technology to enhance workplace safety.

sections.label: Mandatory WSH training call
sections.summary: Companies must ensure safe work environments and equipped, trained and certified workers, and MOM is urged to make WSH training mandatory in high-risk sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This means companies must ensure that the work environment is safe and their workers are equipped with the proper safety equipment and be trained and certified to perform the work activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore urge MOM to make WSH training mandatory for all workers in high-risk sectors.

sections.label: Legislating Company Directors' WSH Code
sections.summary: MOM is developing the Approved Code of Practice for Company Director's WSH Duties, and like Australia, legislating it should be seriously considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MOM is developing the Approved Code of Practice for Company Director’s WSH Duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Like Australia, we should seriously consider legislating the Code so that it will have legislative “teeth”.

sections.label: Elevating WSH Institute
sections.summary: MOM's Workplace Safety and Health Institute focuses on WSH trends and technology partnerships, and MOM is hoped to elevate it into a national WSH Centre of Excellence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MOM currently has the Workplace Safety and Health Institute (WSHI), a department that focuses on WSH trends and partners with stakeholders in the technology ecosystem to improve WSH outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope MOM can elevate the WSH Institute into a national WSH Centre of Excellence.

sections.label: Recent workplace fatality numbers
sections.summary: MOM is extremely concerned about recent workplace fatalities, with 31 since the start of 2022, compared to 37 in 2021 and 39 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MOM is extremely concerned about the recent spate of workplace fatalities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We saw 31 fatalities since the start of 2022, compared to 37 for the whole of 2021 and 39 in 2019 pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Workplace fatality reduction goal
sections.summary: The goal is to reduce workplace fatalities to less than 1 per 100,000 workers by 2028 on a sustainable basis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Our goal remains to reduce workplace fatalities to less than 1 per 100,000 workers by 2028 on a sustainable basis and join just four countries that have achieved this.

sections.label: Directors' WSH duties code
sections.summary: An Approved Code of Practice for Company Directors' WSH Duties will be gazetted later this year to strengthen management commitment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To strengthen management commitment to WSH, we will be gazetting the Approved Code of Practice (ACOP) for Company Directors’ WSH Duties later this year.

sections.label: Reports and enforcement inspections
sections.summary: Of 2,300 reports received in the past 12 months, around 62% of follow-up inspections resulted in enforcements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Out of 2,300 reports received in the past 12 months, around 62% of the follow-up inspections resulted in enforcements taken.

sections.label: Employment Act working hour protections
sections.summary: The Employment Act has existing protections on maximum daily and weekly work hours and maximum monthly overtime hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Member would be aware that there are existing protections under the Employment Act on the maximum number of hours that employees can work per day and per week, as well as the maximum number of overtime hours per month.

sections.label: SMEs WSH technology adoption
sections.summary: SMEs can tap the Productivity Solutions Grant for up to 70% funding of pre-approved solutions, and MOM will work with Government Procurement Entities to include WSH technology in public sector tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: SMEs can tap on the Productivity Solutions Grant to adopt pre-approved solutions with up to 70% funding for qualifying costs, such as the e-Permit-to-Work which allows full visibility of high-risk work activities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To drive greater adoption, MOM will continue to work with the Government Procurement Entities to include suitable WSH technology into public sector tender specifications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The recent spate of accidents has been a setback, but I urge all Members in this House, boards, company leaders, industry associations, union leaders and our workers to continue to play our part in keeping up workplace safety and health.
